title: `radians(x)` is `x * (pi / 180)` and `degrees(x)` is `x * (180 / pi)`, the constants multiplied
verdict: no finding: the constants are rounded first, then one multiplication
description: `radians(x)` equals `x * (pi() / 180)` and `degrees(x)` equals `x * (180 / pi())` for every one of 100,000 random doubles in [-500, 500). The other orders differ: `x * pi() / 180` equals `radians(x)` for 70,736 of them, `x * 180 / pi()` equals `degrees(x)` for 73,772. The SQL lift writes the first form (the constants of `math.pi / 180` and `180 / math.pi`).
reference: The reference's elementary functions of doubles (`Functions.lean`) have no `radians` or `degrees`; the lift writes DuckDB's product (D54).

evidence.sql: select count(*) filter (radians(x)=x*(pi()/180)), count(*) filter (radians(x)=x*pi()/180), count(*) from (select random()*1000-500 x from range(100000))
select count(*) filter (degrees(x)=x*(180/pi())), count(*) filter (degrees(x)=x*180/pi()), count(*) from (select random()*1000-500 x from range(100000))
